title: This “One-in-a-Million” Fossil Has 450-Million-Year-Old Soft Tissue - Nautilus
gist: A Royal Society Open Science study describes a 450-million-year-old crinoid fossil that preserved soft tissue—only the second fossil of its type ever found—a rarity given how quickly soft tissue normally decays.

insights.claim: Soft tissue like skin and organs normally disappears almost immediately after death, requiring rare conditions such as constant refrigeration or a vacuum to be preserved.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Explains why soft-tissue fossils are exceptional and scientifically valuable.
insights.locator: For soft tissue to be preserved, a very specific and rare combination of conditions

insights.claim: Researchers described a 450-million-year-old crinoid fossil (Dendrocrinus simcoensis), a starfish relative, with soft tissue preserved—only the second fossil of its type ever discovered.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: A landmark specimen that could yield rare insight into ancient soft-bodied anatomy.
insights.locator: a 450-million-year-old fossil with soft tissue preserved on it
